mainTopic: Sleeping in תפילין, limits on daytime sleep, and eating small amounts in the סוכה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about sleeping in תפילין. The חכמים allow a short nap (שינת עראי) in תפילין, about the time it takes to walk 100 אמות, but not real sleep. The word 'sleep' leads to רב's rule that no one should sleep during the day longer than a horse sleeps, which is sixty breaths. אביי traces this practice back through great people to דוד המלך, and רב יוסף rebukes אביי for napping longer. The גמרא then returns to תפילין: רבי נתן allows keeping them on for a daytime nap but not at night, and רבי יוסי says young men must always remove them. אביי explains that רבי יוסי's worry is relations with their wives, not impurity itself, and a ברייתא says to wash hands before touching תפילין after such a lapse. A new משנה tells how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל ate even small foods in the סוכה, while רבי צדוק ate a tiny snack outside it. The גמרא asks why a story would contradict the rule. It answers that the משנה is missing a line: a person may be strict with himself without it counting as יוהרא. The supporting story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי יעקב's opinion: hold the strap, not the box
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the opinion of רבי יעקב: the person does not hold the box of the תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not hold the box. These are the words of רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא. We are hearing the last part of רבי יעקב's ruling about a person who was sleeping in his תפילין and had a seminal emission (קרי).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the ברייתא, רבי יעקב said the person may hold the strap of the תפילין. Here he adds that he must not hold the קציצה, the box, which is the holy part. The phrase 'דברי רבי יעקב' signals that his opinion is over and a different view is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: The box of the תפילין that holds the parchments

phrases.english: and he does not hold the box (of the tefillin),
phrases.notes: He may hold the strap, but not the box, which is the holy part.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יעקב, one may hold the strap of the תפילין but not the box.

steps.title: The חכמים: a short nap in תפילין is fine, real sleep is not
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים rule that a person may take a short nap while wearing תפילין, but may not go into a real, settled sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: A person may sleep with תפילין a short nap, but not a settled sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opinion of the חכמים. They let a person nap briefly while wearing תפילין, but they forbid a full sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern with deep sleep in תפילין is that the person might become impure or lose awareness of the holy object. A short nap does not carry that risk, so it is allowed. The key split is between שינת עראי (a brief nap) and שינת קבע (real, settled sleep).

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, the boxes with parchments worn on the arm and head

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
a person may sleep with tefillin a brief nap,
but not a settled sleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that disagrees with רבי יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brief nap in תפילין is permitted, but settled sleep is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of שינת עראי, a short nap, is what leads the גמרא into the next topic about how long a person may sleep during the day.

steps.title: How long is a short nap?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how long a brief nap is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is a brief nap?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how long a 'short nap' lasts. This line sets up the answer that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Short nap' is vague, and a halachic rule needs a clear measure. So the ברייתא asks for a defined length of time.

phrases.english: And how long is a brief nap?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure of the term שינת עראי used in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of a שינת עראי.

steps.title: A short nap is the time to walk 100 cubits
steps.stepSummary: A brief nap lasts as long as it takes to walk one hundred אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as it takes to walk one hundred אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. A short nap is about as long as it takes to walk one hundred אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים measure time by a walking distance, which is common in the תלמוד. Walking one hundred אמות takes only a short moment, so the permitted nap is very brief.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, roughly an arm's length

phrases.english: the time it takes to walk one hundred cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שינת עראי lasts as long as walking 100 אמות.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, you may nap in תפילין only briefly, about the time it takes to walk 100 אמות. Real sleep in תפילין is forbidden.

steps.title: רב: don't sleep during the day longer than a horse sleeps
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that it is forbidden to sleep during the day longer than a horse sleeps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is forbidden for a person to sleep during the day more than the sleep of a horse.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic of short sleep came up, the גמרא brings a related teaching of רב. He limits how long a person may sleep during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule, and it has nothing to do with תפילין. It is about daytime sleep in general. Sleeping too long during the day wastes time that should go to תורה and work, so רב sets a limit: no longer than a horse's sleep.

keyTerms.meaning: The sleep of a horse (a very short sleep)

phrases.english: Rav said:
it is forbidden for a person to sleep during the day
more than the sleep of a horse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought up because of the shared theme of short sleep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not sleep during the day longer than a horse's sleep.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the rule about תפילין. רב is talking about daytime sleep in general, not about sleeping while wearing תפילין.

steps.title: How long does a horse sleep?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a horse's sleep is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is the sleep of a horse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the measure of a 'horse's sleep.' This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with the short nap, the term needs a clear measure before anyone can follow the rule.

phrases.english: And how long is the sleep of a horse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure used in רב's rule.

steps.title: Sixty breaths
steps.stepSummary: A horse's sleep lasts sixty breaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sixty breaths.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that a horse's sleep lasts sixty breaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sixty breaths is only a few minutes. So רב permits only a very short daytime rest.

phrases.english: sixty breaths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A horse's sleep is sixty breaths.

steps.title: אביי's chain: great people who slept like a horse
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a chain: his teacher slept like רב, רב like רבי, רבי like דוד המלך, and דוד like a horse, which is sixty breaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The sleep of the Master (רבה) was like that of רב, and that of רב like that of רבי, and that of רבי like that of דוד, and that of דוד like a horse's, and a horse's is sixty breaths.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows that רב's rule was actually practiced by great people. Each one followed the one before him, all the way back to דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מר' here means רבה, אביי's teacher. The chain shows that the sixty-breath limit was a real practice handed down through the generations, going back to דוד, who barely slept. It supports רב's rule with a tradition of how the great people actually lived.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
the sleep of the Master was like that of Rav,
and that of Rav was like that of Rabbi,
and that of Rabbi was like that of David,
and that of David was like that of a horse,
and that of a horse is sixty breaths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's rule with a chain of practice by great people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great people from דוד onward limited their daytime sleep to sixty breaths.

steps.title: אביי slept for the length of a short walk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא relates that אביי would sleep during the day for about the time it takes to walk from פומבדיתא to בי כובי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would sleep for as long as it takes to go from פומבדיתא to בי כובי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about אביי. He slept during the day longer than the horse's sleep, about the time of a short trip between two nearby places. This story sets up רב יוסף's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though אביי himself reported the sixty-breath tradition, his own nap was longer than that. This gap is what bothers רב יוסף next.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major תורה center in בבל
בי כובי, a place near פומבדיתא

phrases.english: Abaye would sleep
for as long as it takes to go from Pumbedita to Bei Kuvei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about אביי's own sleep after his teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's daytime nap lasted about the length of the trip from פומבדיתא to בי כובי.

steps.title: רב יוסף criticizes אביי with a verse about the lazy person
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף applied the פסוק 'How long will you lie down, lazy one?' to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף read about him: 'How long will you lie down, lazy one? When will you get up from your sleep?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף, אביי's teacher, criticizes אביי for sleeping too long by quoting a פסוק from משלי about the lazy person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a rebuke of behavior rather than a question about a text. It shows that sleeping longer than the horse's sleep was treated as wasted time that should have gone to learning תורה. The story ends the section by confirming how seriously the limit was taken.

keyTerms.meaning: He read (a פסוק) about him, i.e., applied it to him

phrases.english: Rav Yosef read about him:
"How long, lazy one, will you lie down?
phrases.notes: This is a פסוק from משלי 6:9.

phrases.english: When will you get up from your sleep?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts critically to the story in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's practice of sleeping longer than sixty breaths.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sleeping beyond the horse's sleep is laziness and takes away from learning תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב limits daytime sleep to a horse's sleep (sixty breaths). Great people kept this limit, and even אביי was rebuked by רב יוסף for napping longer.

steps.title: Sleeping in תפילין: day versus night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי נתן's view. When napping during the day, a person may keep his תפילין on or take them off. At night he must remove them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Someone who lies down to sleep during the day may take off his תפילין if he wants, or leave them on if he wants. At night, he takes them off and may not leave them on. These are the words of רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: Having just discussed daytime naps, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about whether a person may sleep while wearing תפילין. רבי נתן gives a different rule for day and for night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daytime nap is usually short and light, so there is less worry that the person will act in a way that shows disrespect to the תפילין. A night's sleep is long and deep, so he must take them off. Night is also not the normal time for wearing תפילין at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves on, or puts on (the תפילין)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who goes in to sleep during the day,
if he wants, he removes them; if he wants, he leaves them on.
At night, he removes them and does not leave them on,
these are the words of רבי נתן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of daytime napping to the related הלכה of sleeping while wearing תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By day, a person may choose whether to remove his תפילין before sleeping. At night, he must remove them.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: young men must always remove them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that young men must always take off their תפילין before sleeping, even during the day, because they are prone to impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Young men always take them off and do not leave them on, because they commonly become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא adds a stricter rule for young men. They must always remove their תפילין before sleeping, day or night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that young men are 'used to impurity.' This means they are more likely to have a seminal emission (קרי) while asleep. This reason will trigger the next question in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Always (here: both by day and by night)
Accustomed to impurity, meaning likely to experience קרי

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Young men always remove them and do not leave them on,
because they are accustomed to impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הַיְּלָדִים, לְעוֹלָם חוֹלְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the same ברייתא, which is stricter for young men.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young men must always remove their תפילין before sleeping, because they are prone to impurity.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי forbid תפילין to one who had an emission?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי's reason implies a בעל קרי may not wear תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי יוסי holds that a בעל קרי is forbidden to put on תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks what רבי יוסי's reason implies. It suggests that he must hold a בעל קרי may not wear תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only worry were becoming impure from קרי, then רבי יוסי would be saying that impurity itself makes תפילין forbidden. That is a big and questionable claim. The 'shall we say' form signals that the גמרא wants to push back on this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? This introduces a suggested inference, usually one the גמרא will reject.
A man who has had a seminal emission

phrases.english: Shall we say that רבי יוסי holds
that a בעל קרי is forbidden to put on תפילין?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problematic conclusion from the reason רבי יוסי gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's reason, 'because they are accustomed to impurity'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If impurity is the reason for removing תפילין, then רבי יוסי must hold that a בעל קרי may not wear תפילין. That would be a sweeping and questionable position.

steps.title: אביי: the worry is young men sleeping with their wives
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the case involves young men whose wives are with them. The worry is that they may come to have relations while still wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We are dealing with young men whose wives are with them. The worry is that they might come to do what they are used to doing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the suggestion. He says רבי יוסי was not talking about impurity itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the 'impurity' in the ברייתא refers to marital relations. If a young man sleeps beside his wife while wearing תפילין, he may forget them and have relations, which disgraces the תפילין. So רבי יוסי never claimed that a בעל קרי may not wear תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (a specific case)
A habitual matter. Here this is a gentle way of referring to marital relations.
Lest, perhaps. This introduces a worry.

phrases.english: אביי said:
We are dealing with young men whose wives are with them,
lest they come to their habitual matter.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that רבי יוסי forbids תפילין to a בעל קרי. אביי's whole point is that the ברייתא is about the risk of relations while wearing תפילין, not about impurity itself.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בִּילָדִים וּנְשׁוֹתֵיהֶן עִמָּהֶן עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion by narrowing the case that רבי יוסי was discussing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case and the reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's concern was impurity from קרי, which would imply that a בעל קרי may not wear תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern is young men sleeping with their wives, who might have relations while wearing תפילין. Nothing can be proven about a בעל קרי.

steps.title: Wash hands before removing תפילין after relations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches what to do if someone forgot and had relations while wearing תפילין. He may not touch the straps or the box until he washes his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he forgot and had relations while wearing תפילין, he may not hold either the strap or the box until he washes his hands and then removes them, because hands are busy.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about a person who forgot he was wearing תפילין and had relations. It tells him how to remove them respectfully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hands tend to touch unclean parts of the body without the person noticing. So before handling the תפילין, he must wash his hands. This applies to both the straps (רצועה) and the box (קציצה).

keyTerms.meaning: Busy hands, which touch things without the person noticing

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he forgot and had relations while wearing תפילין,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹחֵז לֹא בָּרְצוּעָה וְלֹא בַּקְּצִיצָה
phrases.english: he may not hold either the strap or the box
until he washes his hands, and then removes them,
because hands are busy.

steps.whatToRemember: The תפילין discussion here centers on respect. Do not sleep in them where there is a real risk of disgracing them, and wash your hands before touching them after relations.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁכַח וְשִׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בִּתְפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from אביי's case of relations while wearing תפילין and tells what to do if it actually happened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After forgetting and having relations while wearing תפילין, a person must wash his hands before touching the straps or the box to remove them.

steps.title: New משנה: sages bring even small foods to the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה tells of an incident. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was brought a cooked dish to taste, and רבן גמליאל was brought two dates and a bucket of water. Both said to take the food up to the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There was an incident where they brought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי a cooked dish to taste, and they brought רבן גמליאל two dates and a bucket of water. They said: Bring them up to the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the topic of the סוכה with a new משנה. It tells a story of two great sages who insisted on eating even small amounts of food in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה allowed a small snack outside the סוכה. In this story, both sages chose to eat even a taste of food, or dates and water, inside the סוכה. The גמרא will next analyze what this story proves.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story told to teach a הלכה
Take them up to the סוכה

phrases.english: משנה: There was an incident, and they brought

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לִטְעוֹם אֶת הַתַּבְשִׁיל,
phrases.english: to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי a cooked dish to taste,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שְׁנֵי כּוֹתָבוֹת וּדְלִי שֶׁל מַיִם.
phrases.english: and to רבן גמליאל two dates and a bucket of water.
And they said: Take them up to the סוכה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This story sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of whether eating small amounts in the סוכה is required or is an extra stringency.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַעֲשֶׂה וְהֵבִיאוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion of sleep and תפילין and begins a new משנה about eating in the סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל had even a small dish, or dates and water, taken up to the סוכה to eat there.

steps.title: רבי צדוק eats a tiny snack outside the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a contrasting story. רבי צדוק was given less than an egg's worth of food. He held it with a cloth, ate it outside the סוכה, and did not say a blessing afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they gave רבי צדוק less than an egg-size amount of food, he took it with a napkin, ate it outside the סוכה, and did not say a blessing after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a second story. This one shows the lenient side: a very small amount of food may be eaten outside the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Less than a כביצה counts as a snack, not a meal. So רבי צדוק did not need a סוכה and did not need to wash his hands (he used a cloth for cleanliness). He also said no blessing afterward, because such a small amount does not count as being satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an egg; the minimum amount that counts as a real meal here
He took it with a cloth or napkin, instead of washing his hands
And he did not say a blessing after eating it (no ברכה אחרונה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי צדוק was being careless. Each thing he did follows a rule for amounts smaller than a כביצה.

phrases.english: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok
food less than an egg-bulk,
he took it with a cloth,
phrases.notes: Instead of washing his hands, which is not required for less than an egg-bulk

phrases.english: and he ate it outside the sukkah,
and he did not bless after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a lenient story that contrasts with the strict story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Less than a כביצה of food may be eaten outside the סוכה, without washing hands, and without a ברכה אחרונה.

steps.title: Why tell a story that contradicts the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה brings a story that seems to go against its own rule that snacks may be eaten outside the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is the משנה bringing a story to contradict its own rule?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a challenge to the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said casual eating outside the סוכה is allowed. But the story shows רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל insisting on taking even a taste or two dates into the סוכה. A story is supposed to support the rule, not argue with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A story brought to contradict the rule

phrases.english: GEMARA:
An incident to contradict?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the story in the משנה fits with the rule before it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל in the משנה (step 16)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows snacks outside the סוכה, yet its story shows great rabbis refusing to eat even a little outside. A story should not contradict the rule it comes with.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: being strict is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing a line. The full version says that if someone wants to be strict on himself, he may, and it is not considered showing off.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing something, and this is what it teaches: If a person wants to be strict with himself, he may be strict, and it is not showing off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adding a missing line to the משנה. That line makes the story fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic law stays the same: a snack may be eaten outside the סוכה. The added line says a person may choose to be stricter, and this is not arrogance (יוהרא). Now the story shows a permitted extra strictness, not a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing from the text
And this is how it teaches (the full text)
To be strict on oneself, beyond what the law requires
Arrogance or showing off with extra piety

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not cancel the rule that snacks are allowed outside the סוכה. It only adds that being stricter is a fine personal choice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic principle that adding a personal stringency in סוכה is not considered יוהרא.

phrases.english: It is lacking (something),
and this is what it teaches:
If he comes to be stringent on himself —
he may be stringent,
and there is no presumptuousness in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by adding a missing line to the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (חסורי מחסרא): adding a missing clause to the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to show that snacking outside the סוכה is forbidden, which contradicts the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Snacking outside is allowed, but someone who chooses to be strict may do so without it counting as יוהרא. The story illustrates that stringency.

steps.title: The story re-read as support for being strict
steps.stepSummary: In its corrected form, the משנה brings the story again as support: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was brought a dish to taste, and רבן גמליאל two dates and a bucket of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was also a story: they brought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי a cooked dish to taste, and they brought רבן גמליאל two dates and a bucket of water,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the story from the משנה, but now it is part of the corrected text and backs up the new line about being strict. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the story looked like it argued with the rule. Now, with the words 'and there was also a story', it becomes proof that great rabbis chose to be strict, which is allowed. The words are the same, but their job has changed.

keyTerms.meaning: And there was also a story (supporting the ruling)

phrases.english: And there was also an incident:

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵבִיאוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: and they brought to Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
a cooked dish to taste,
and to Rabban Gamliel
two dates and a bucket of water,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the corrected text from step 19 and re-reads the story from step 16 as support for the stringency.
steps.raayaObject: The added rule that a person may be strict on himself without it being יוהרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל taking even small amounts of food into the סוכה
